name: Background symmetry
definition: Symmetric, mildly asymmetric, or markedly asymmetric background.
criteria: Mild: consistent voltage difference <50% on an appropriate referential recording or frequency difference 0.5–1 Hz.
Marked: voltage difference >=50% or frequency difference >1 Hz.
Consistent means >80% of relevant instances or record.
context: Non-neonatal EEG; report A.2–A.10 separately by hemisphere when asymmetric.
pitfalls: Do not measure voltage symmetry from longitudinal bipolar amplitude when referential comparison is unavailable.
engineering: Choose the amplitude statistic and epoch aggregation for percent difference.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Predominant background frequency
definition: Band or tied bands most prominent when maximally awake or after stimulation.
criteria: Categories: beta >13 Hz, alpha, theta, delta.
Report all 2 or 3 bands when equally prominent.
context: Non-neonatal EEG; some terms may be imperfect for infants.
pitfalls: Do not substitute a less-alert state when a more-awake/stimulated state is available.
engineering: S01 gives no alpha/theta/delta boundaries or tie tolerance; version and review these separately.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Posterior dominant rhythm
definition: Posterior dominant rhythm present with frequency, absent, or unclear.
criteria: Present requires attenuation with eye opening.
Wait >1 s after eye closure before measuring frequency; report to nearest 0.5 Hz.
context: Non-neonatal EEG with interpretable eye-opening/closure testing.
pitfalls: A posterior rhythm without demonstrated eye-opening attenuation is not present by this definition.
engineering: Define attenuation threshold and minimum observation duration; S01 does not.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Continuity and low-voltage percent
definition: Continuity category from percent of a record/epoch occupied by attenuation or suppression.
criteria: Attenuation: lower activity >=10 µV and <50% of higher-voltage background; suppression: lower activity <10 µV.
Continuous: low-voltage percent <1%.
Nearly continuous: 1–9%, with qualifying periods >=1 s; report typical duration.
Discontinuous: alternating higher activity with 10–49% attenuation/suppression.
Burst attenuation/suppression: alternating higher activity with 50–99% attenuation/suppression.
Suppression/attenuation: >99%; suppressed when all activity <10 µV, attenuated when all activity <20 µV but not suppressed.
For noncontinuous records report attenuation or suppression percent using record/epoch as denominator.
Stimulus-induced periods are SI-attenuation or SI-suppression.
context: Non-neonatal EEG; these voltage cutoffs differ from neonatal terminology.
pitfalls: >99% is not discontinuous or burst attenuation/suppression.
engineering: Fix analysis epoch, boundaries, and handling of mixed attenuation plus suppression.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Burst attenuation/suppression modifiers
definition: Timing, localization, morphology, highly epileptiform, and identical-burst descriptors.
criteria: Burst averages >=0.5 s and has >=4 phases (>=3 baseline crossings); maximum duration 30 s.
Report location as generalized, lateralized, bilateral independent, unilateral independent, or multifocal; report typical burst/interburst durations and sharpest component.

Highly epileptiform: >=2 spikes/sharp waves in most (>50%) bursts at mean >=1 Hz within a burst, where frequency = 1 / typical interpeak latency; alternatively a rhythmic potentially ictal-appearing pattern occurs in most (>50%) bursts. Table 1 states >=1 Hz for this alternative, while A.4.d does not repeat that cutoff. Record frequency and location.
Identical: first >=0.5 s of each burst, or each stereotyped cluster of >=2 bursts, is visually similar in all channels in most (>90%) bursts.
context: Only burst attenuation or burst suppression.
pitfalls: Shorter or <4-phase events are discharges.
RPP, BIRD, and seizure classification is outside this contract.
engineering: Resolve the Table 1/A.4.d frequency-cutoff discrepancy; operationalize visual similarity and potentially ictal appearance.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Background reactivity
definition: Cerebral response to stimulation: reactive, unreactive, SIRPIDs-only, unclear, or unknown.
criteria: Qualifying change may be in cerebral voltage or frequency, including attenuation.
SIRPIDs-only: sole response is a stimulus-induced rhythmic, periodic, or ictal-appearing discharge.
Unclear: inadequate test, excessive artifact, or equivocal cerebral change. Unknown: not tested or maximally alert throughout.
context: Non-neonatal EEG with documented stimulation.
pitfalls: Muscle activity and eye blinks do not establish reactivity.
engineering: Define stimulation protocol and cerebral-change threshold; S01 does not fully specify them.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: State changes and N2 transients
definition: Sustained alertness/stimulation-related backgrounds with separate N2-transient characterization.
criteria: Present requires >=2 background types, each sustained >=60 s.
Stimulation should transition less-alert to more-alert/stimulated; spontaneous transitions qualify; the more-alert state is primary.
State changes virtually always imply reactivity; reactivity need not imply a state change when it lasts <60 s.
Categories: present with normal N2 transients; present with abnormal N2 transients; present without N2 transients; absent.
Describe K-complexes and spindles separately: present-normal, present-abnormal with abnormality, or absent.
context: Non-neonatal EEG; spontaneous or stimulated transitions.
pitfalls: Reactivity lasting <60 s does not alone establish a state change.
engineering: Define persistence across brief artifact and structured N2 abnormalities.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Cyclic alternating pattern of encephalopathy
definition: Regular spontaneous alternation of two backgrounds: present, absent, or unknown/unclear.
criteria: Each pattern lasts >=10 s and the pair alternates spontaneously/regularly for >=6 complete cycles; a cycle includes each state once.
Describe each pattern and typical duration; note awake/stimulated versus less-awake state when known.
If each pattern lasts >60 s, state-change criteria are also met.
context: Non-neonatal encephalopathic EEG; components may include separately classified RPPs.
pitfalls: Stimulus-driven alternation alone is not the stated definition.
engineering: Define tolerance for 'regular'; S01 does not.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Background voltage
definition: High, normal, low, or suppressed peak-to-trough background voltage.
criteria: High: most/all activity >=150 µV.
Low: most/all activity <20 µV but not suppressed.
Suppressed: all activity <10 µV.
For nearly continuous/discontinuous records, use the higher-voltage portion.
context: Non-neonatal standard 10–20 longitudinal bipolar EEG.
pitfalls: Do not apply to neonatal EEG.
engineering: Define 'most/all' and numeric normal bounds; S01 does not.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Anterior-posterior gradient
definition: Expected AP gradient present, absent, or reversed.
criteria: Present: clear persistent segment >=1 continuous min with lower-voltage/faster anterior and higher-voltage/slower posterior activity.
Reversed: same duration and paired criteria in the opposite direction.
context: Non-neonatal EEG with anterior and posterior derivations.
pitfalls: Voltage-only or frequency-only gradient is insufficient.
engineering: Define quantitative 'clear' threshold.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Breach effect
definition: Breach effect present with location, absent, or unclear.
criteria: Present: higher amplitude and increased sharpness, mainly faster frequencies, versus the rest of brain and especially the contralateral homologous region.
context: EEG over or near a skull defect.
pitfalls: Sharp activity without the skull-defect spatial relationship is insufficient.
engineering: Define comparison thresholds and whether defect metadata is mandatory.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Sporadic epileptiform discharge morphology
definition: Nonrhythmic, nonperiodic spikes, sharp waves, and polyspikes.
criteria: Spike: pointed transient distinct from background, duration >=20 ms and <70 ms at EEG baseline.
Sharp wave: same definition, duration >=70 ms and <=200 ms (source states 70–200 ms).
Polyspike: >=2 consecutive spikes with no interdischarge interval, total duration <0.5 s.
Typical, not required: diphasic/triphasic, apiculate, asymmetric slope, followed by slow wave or other background disruption.
context: Non-neonatal EEG; localization may be added.
pitfalls: Rhythmic/periodic discharges are not sporadic.
>=0.5-s spike trains may enter BIRD or highly epileptiform burst classification, outside scope.
engineering: S01 does not quantify pointedness/background disruption or explicitly discuss the 200-ms endpoint; adjudicate boundary cases.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Sporadic epileptiform discharge prevalence
definition: Combined prevalence of spikes, polyspikes, and sharp waves.
criteria: Abundant: >=1/10 s, but not periodic.
Frequent: >=1/min and <1/10 s.
Occasional: >=1/h and <1/min.
Rare: <1/h.
When abundant, mean and maximum count per 10-s epoch may be recorded.
context: Nonrhythmic, nonperiodic sporadic discharges in non-neonatal EEG.
pitfalls: Periodic discharges cannot be abundant sporadic discharges.
engineering: S01 provides no explicit absent category; represent zero events separately pending review.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: RPP term construction and validity boundary
definition: An RPP name combines one localization main term with one pattern-type main term, then adds applicable modifiers.

criteria.frequency_boundary: No RPP may have a typical frequency above 4 Hz. A pattern above 4 Hz lasting at least 0.5 s is outside this RPP contract; one shorter than 0.5 s is not an RPP.
criteria.evolution_boundary: Within RPP terminology, evolution is limited to patterns at or below 4 Hz and shorter than 10 s. Longer evolving patterns and faster short patterns are delegated to the seizure/BIRD contracts.

context: All RPP labels in this file.
pitfalls: ESz/ESE/ECSz/ECSE definitions
BIRD definitions
IIC derivations
engineering: Represent boundary handoffs as validation failures or external labels; do not derive seizure, BIRD, or IIC labels here.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Main term 1: localization
definition: Main term 1 specifies the spatial organization of the RPP.

G.name: Generalized
G.rule: Bilaterally synchronous and symmetric, including a restricted field. Bilateral asymmetry or asynchrony that shifts and is not consistently lateralized to one side more than 80% of the time remains G.

predominance.frontally: anterior voltage at least 50% greater than posterior
predominance.occipitally: posterior voltage at least 50% greater than anterior
predominance.midline: midline voltage at least 50% greater than parasagittal
predominance.not_otherwise_specified: similar voltage in all regions and none of the preceding

qualifiers.asynchrony: For shifting asynchrony, record typical inter-side lag.

L.name: Lateralized
L.rule: Unilateral; or bilateral with clearly and consistently greater amplitude on one side; or bilateral with a consistent lead-in from one side. Includes focal, regional, and hemispheric patterns.

qualifiers.consistency: Bilateral asymmetric and bilateral asynchronous examples require the same side more than 80% of the time.
qualifiers.lag: For bilateral asynchronous, record typical inter-side lag.

BI.name: Bilateral independent
BI.rule: Two independent, therefore asynchronous, lateralized patterns, one in each hemisphere, occurring simultaneously (overlapping in time), not sequentially.

symmetry: asymmetric with L > R or R > L

UI.name: Unilateral independent
UI.rule: Two independent, therefore asynchronous, periodic or rhythmic patterns in the same hemisphere occurring simultaneously, not sequentially. A focal midline pattern can be ipsilateral to an independent left or right pattern.

Mf.name: Multifocal
Mf.rule: At least three independent lateralized patterns, with at least one in each hemisphere, all occurring simultaneously.

symmetry: asymmetric with L > R or R > L

context: All PD, RDA, and SW patterns.
pitfalls: Independent patterns occurring at different times are separate lateralized patterns, not BI or UI.
Two lateralized sides with fixed interhemispheric latency are lateralized bilateral-asynchronous, not BI.
engineering: Store the main term and qualifiers independently; do not infer localization from a single channel label.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Main term 2: PDs, RDA, and SW
definition: Main term 2 specifies the repeating waveform organization.

PDs.name: Periodic discharges
PDs.rule: Relatively uniform waveform morphology and duration, a discernible inter-discharge interval, and recurrence at nearly regular intervals.
PDs.regularity: Cycle length varies by less than 50% from one cycle to the next in a majority (>50%) of cycle pairs.
PDs.discharge: Waveform shorter than 0.5 s irrespective of phases, or at least 0.5 s with no more than 3 phases; must stand out from background.

RDA.name: Rhythmic delta activity
RDA.rule: Relatively uniform waveform morphology and duration with no interval between waves; irregular or polymorphic delta is not RDA.
RDA.regularity: Period varies by less than 50% from the subsequent cycle in a majority (>50%) of cycle pairs.
RDA.note: Sharp crests or troughs do not prevent a pattern from being rhythmic.

SW.name: Spike-and-wave or sharp-and-wave
SW.rule: Spike, polyspike, or sharp wave consistently followed by a slow wave in a regular alternating repeating pattern, with a consistent component relationship for at least 6 consecutive cycles and no interval between complexes.

context: RPPs after main-term-1 localization is assigned.
pitfalls: An interval between spike-wave complexes is PDs, with each discharge a spike-and-wave.
A pattern qualifying as both PDs and RDA is PDs+R, not RDA+S.
engineering: Preserve source categories as enums; do not collapse PD, RDA, and SW into a generic rhythmicity class.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Prevalence, duration, and frequency modifiers
definition: These modifiers quantify how much pattern is present, its continuous run length, and its rate.

prevalence_percent_record_or_epoch.denominator: proportion of the record or epoch that includes or is within the pattern; intervals between widely spaced PDs count as pattern duration
prevalence_percent_record_or_epoch.multiple_patterns: Record each pattern and its own prevalence.

frequency_hz.PD_SW_restriction: Typical frequency >2.5 Hz is an RPP only when duration is <10 s; at >=10 s it is outside this RPP contract.

context: All RPPs; duration is recorded if not continuous.
pitfalls: Do not calculate seizure burden here.
Do not recast frequency-boundary patterns as seizure/BIRD labels in this contract.
engineering: Store numeric measurements and categorical bins together so bins remain auditable.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Phases, sharpness, and voltage modifiers
definition: These modifiers describe discharge structure, contour, and amplitude.

phases.formula: 1 + number of baseline crossings of the typical discharge
phases.montage: longitudinal bipolar, channel where most apparent
phases.baseline_rule: Start and end points are not crossings

sharpness.spiky: component duration at EEG baseline <70 ms
sharpness.sharply_contoured: steep slope on one side and/or pointed/apiculate inflection, but too long to be sharp
sharpness.required: Describe dominant (highest-voltage) phase and sharpest phase if different.

absolute_voltage_peak_to_trough_uV.montage: standard longitudinal bipolar 10-20, channel where pattern is most apparent

criteria.relative_voltage_PDs_only: Ratio of the highest-voltage component of the typical discharge to typical between-discharge background in the same channel and montage; bin as <=2 or >2.

context: Phases: PDs and the entire SW complex, not RDA. Sharpness and polarity: PDs and spike/sharp component of SW, not RDA. Voltage: PDs, SW, and RDA; relative voltage only PDs.
pitfalls: Do not use background EEG voltage for the RPP voltage modifier.
engineering: Retain the acquisition montage with every amplitude, phase, and polarity-related field.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Stimulus state, evolution, fluctuation, and static modifiers
definition: Stimulus modifiers describe reproducible response to alerting stimulation; temporal modifiers describe frequency, morphology, or location change.

stimulus_state.SI: Reproducibly brought about or exacerbated by alerting stimulus in a less-stimulated state, with or without clinical alerting; may also occur spontaneously.
stimulus_state.ST: Reproducibly terminated or attenuated by alerting stimulus in a less-stimulated state, with or without clinical alerting; may also self-terminate.
stimulus_state.spontaneous: Never clearly induced, exacerbated, improved, or terminated by stimulation.

evolving.minimum: At least 2 unequivocal sequential changes in the same category.
evolving.frequency: Two consecutive changes in one direction, each at least 0.5 Hz; each frequency persists at least 3 cycles.
evolving.morphology: Two consecutive novel morphologies; each morphology, including transition forms, persists at least 3 cycles.
evolving.location: Sequential spread into or out of at least 2 standard 10-20 electrode locations; involvement of each additional electrode persists at least 3 cycles.
evolving.interstep_gap: Reach criteria without the changing feature remaining unchanged for 5 or more continuous minutes.
evolving.amplitude: Voltage/amplitude change alone is neither evolution nor a new morphology.

fluctuating.minimum: At least 3 changes, no more than 1 minute apart, not qualifying as evolution.
fluctuating.frequency: Each change at least 0.5 Hz; each frequency persists at least 3 cycles.
fluctuating.morphology: Each morphology persists at least 3 cycles.
fluctuating.location: Each change at least 1 standard interelectrode distance; each location persists at least 3 cycles.
fluctuating.amplitude: Voltage/amplitude change alone is not fluctuation.

criteria.additional_reporting: If evolving or fluctuating in frequency, specify minimum and maximum frequency. For nongeneralized patterns specify spread as none, unilateral, or bilateral.

context: Stimulus state applies to RPPs. Evolution/fluctuation/static applies to RPPs within the RPP validity boundary.
pitfalls: SIRPIDs is an umbrella source term; record the specific SI-RPP rather than deriving seizure/IIC/BIRD forms.
No seizure/BIRD/IIC classification is emitted.
engineering: Use an event sequence rather than a single classifier score so cycle persistence, direction, and interstep gap can be audited.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Plus modifier and extreme delta brush
definition: Plus denotes an added feature that makes PDs or RDA more ictal-appearing than the unmodified pattern. Extreme delta brush is a specific +F subtype.

subtypes.+F: Superimposed theta-or-faster activity, rhythmic or not, on PDs or RDA. It must be part of the pattern, not merely background; for PDs it may be continuous if absent when PDs are absent, or occur regularly with each discharge.
subtypes.+R: Superimposed rhythmic or quasi-rhythmic delta activity; PDs only.
subtypes.+S: Associated sharp waves, spikes, or sharp contour; RDA only; present at least once per 10 s and not an SW pattern.

criteria.bilateral_rule: If a bilateral pattern qualifies for plus on only one side, the overall main term still receives the plus modifier.

EDB.definite: Abundant or continuous RDA+F with fast activity stereotypically related to the delta wave, or abundant/continuous PDs+F where each PD is a single blunt delta wave and fast activity is stereotypically related to that delta wave.
EDB.possible: Meets either EDB form but is only occasional/frequent, or the fast activity lacks a stereotyped delta-wave relationship.
EDB.not_EDB: RDA+F/PDs+F lacking both required EDB conditions; a periodic pattern can be EDB only if PDs are blunt delta brushes; fast activity between delta waves or present as background does not qualify.

context: Plus applies to PDs and RDA only, never SW.
pitfalls: Other ictal-appearing attributes, including sharpness, voltage, and fluctuation, are reported through their own modifiers.
engineering: Encode plus subtypes as a set and EDB as a separately validated subtype; do not infer EDB from +F alone.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Minor modifiers
definition: Minor modifiers refine onset, morphology, lag, and polarity.

criteria.triphasic_morphology: Three negative-positive-negative phases, each longer than the preceding and the positive phase of highest voltage; or positive-negative biphasic appearance when a low-voltage first negative phase is obscured by background. PDs and SW only.
criteria.anterior_posterior_lag: Consistent measurable delay >100 ms from most anterior to most posterior derivation, or reverse; report typical anterior-to-posterior delay in ms (negative for posterior-to-anterior) in longitudinal bipolar and referential montage, preferably ipsilateral-ear reference. PDs or spike/sharp component of SW only.

polarity.rule: Describe dominant/highest-voltage phase in a referential montage; PDs or spike/sharp component of SW only.

context: As specified per modifier.
pitfalls: Triphasic morphology, lag, and polarity do not apply to RDA.
engineering: Keep conventional terminology and raw lag in milliseconds together; do not infer polarity from bipolar montage.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Electrographic seizure
definition: An EEG event that meets the ACNS electrographic seizure criteria through discharge rate or definite evolution and duration.
criteria: Either discharges averaging >2.5 Hz for >=10 s (>25 discharges/10 s), OR a pattern with definite evolution lasting >=10 s.
Sharply contoured discharges >200 ms may qualify through the high-rate pathway even when not technically epileptiform.
Evolution must satisfy the source RPP evolution criteria; amplitude change alone is insufficient.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review

pitfalls: Do not infer neonatal seizure criteria from this contract
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Electrographic status epilepticus
definition: Electrographic seizures meeting the ACNS continuous-duration or cumulative hourly-burden criteria for status.
criteria: Qualifying ESz continues for >=10 minutes, OR total ESz duration is >=20% of any 60-minute interval.
Hourly burden uses the specified 60-minute denominator, not a cropped display's duration.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Enough recording for the continuous-duration branch or a 60-minute burden window

status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Electroclinical seizure
definition: An EEG pattern with a definite time-linked clinical correlate, or both EEG and clinical improvement after parenteral antiseizure medication.
criteria: An EEG pattern with a definite time-locked clinical correlate, OR EEG AND clinical improvement after parenteral antiseizure medication.
A definite correlate must accompany the pattern and be absent when that pattern is absent; subtle signs can qualify.
Duration <10 s qualifies only with a definite clinical correlate. An ECSz need not meet ESz; report both when both qualify.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Clinical event/video evidence or documented EEG and clinical medication response

pitfalls: Muscle artifact synthesized beside an event is not proof of a clinical correlate
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Electroclinical status epilepticus
definition: Electroclinical seizures meeting status-duration or hourly-burden criteria, with a separate threshold for ongoing bilateral tonic-clonic activity.
criteria: ECSz persists >=10 continuous minutes OR occupies >=20% of any 60-minute interval.
Exception: ongoing bilateral tonic-clonic motor seizure qualifies at >=5 continuous minutes.

Known epileptic encephalopathy additionally requires increased prominence/frequency of discharges from baseline with clinical deterioration, OR EEG and clinical improvement following parenteral antiseizure medication.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Clinical state, baseline in known epileptic encephalopathy, treatment/response timing where used

status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Possible electroclinical status epilepticus
definition: A qualifying prolonged ictal-interictal continuum pattern that improves electrographically after parenteral antiseizure medication without clinical improvement.
criteria: An IIC RPP persists >=10 continuous minutes OR >=20% of any 60-minute interval.
Parenteral antiseizure medication improves the EEG without clinical improvement.
All duration, IIC and response requirements are conjunctive.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Medication route/time and separate EEG versus clinical response

pitfalls: Already qualifying ESz/ESE excluded
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Nonconvulsive seizure/status qualifier
definition: A qualifier indicating that a seizure or status event lacks prominent motor activity; it does not mean there is no clinical correlate.
criteria: No prominent motor activity; applies to electrographic or electroclinical seizure/status.
Prefer nonconvulsive to subclinical: absence of prominent movement does not establish absence of clinical contribution.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Clinical motor observations; cannot be inferred from EEG alone

status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Stimulus-induced seizure/IIC/BIRDs qualifier
definition: A qualifier for a qualifying pattern reproducibly induced or exacerbated by an alerting stimulus.
criteria: Alerting stimulus reproducibly induces or exacerbates the qualifying phenomenon; prepend SI to the qualifying term.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Stimulus timestamps and responses; distinguish artifact

pitfalls: Temporal proximity alone without reproducibility is insufficient
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Brief potentially ictal rhythmic discharges
definition: Brief potentially ictal rhythmic discharges with specified frequency, duration and morphology/context requirements.
criteria: Focal (L/BI/UI/Mf) or generalized rhythmic activity >4 Hz, at least six waves at a regular rate, duration >=0.5 s and <10 s.
Exclude known normal/benign patterns, activity forming part of burst-suppression/attenuation, and definite clinical correlates.
Definite: evolution OR morphology AND location resembling interictal discharges or seizures in the same patient.
Possible: sharply contoured without either definite criterion.
Paroxysmal fast activity of the stated duration can qualify, focal or generalized, subject to the defining exclusions.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Same-patient comparative EEG if similarity branch is used

pitfalls: Do not equate neonatal BRDs with this definition
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Ictal-interictal continuum
definition: EEG patterns that do not meet definite seizure criteria but may contribute to impaired alertness, symptoms or neuronal injury in the appropriate clinical context.
criteria: Always exclude ESz/ESE.
Pathway A: PD/SW averages >1 and <=2.5 Hz over 10 s.
Pathway B: PD/SW averages >=0.5 and <=1 Hz over 10 s AND (has a plus modifier OR fluctuation).
Pathway C: lateralized RDA averages >1 Hz for >=10 s AND (has a plus modifier OR fluctuation); includes LRDA, BIRDA, UIRDA and MfRDA.
IIC describes an electrographic category, not a diagnosis or an automatic treatment order.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Full clinical context for interpretation; only waveform category is derived here

pitfalls: GRDA does not qualify through pathway C
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Minimum clinical reporting context
definition: Recommended review, communication and reporting context for critical-care EEG.
criteria: Review/report first 30–60 minutes promptly.
Written report at least once per 24 hours; significant intervening changes get separate epochs/reports.
Communication updates at least twice daily recommended except unusually stable circumstances.

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Clinical-care reporting recommendation; not a synthetic waveform criterion

status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Pattern/seizure burden and index
definition: Measures of the duration or frequency-weighted duration of a pattern over an explicitly defined reporting interval.
criteria: Daily burden: total pattern or seizure duration per 24 hours; hourly and maximal hourly burdens also reportable.
Daily pattern index: daily burden multiplied by mean frequency; retain units (Hz-hours or Hz-minutes).

context.setting: critical care; other settings with contextual review
required_context: Observation interval and interpretable duration must be retained; do not treat missing EEG as absence

engineering: Union overlapping intervals for occupied time; declare missing-data denominator policy in P3 rather than invent it as ACNS rule.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Neonatal recording context and daily reporting
definition: Minimum context needed to interpret each 24-hour neonatal continuous video-EEG period and its clinically relevant changes.
criteria: Record postmenstrual age (PMA) at acquisition; PMA is gestational age from last menstrual period plus chronological age.
Source categories are preterm <37 weeks PMA, term 37 up to 44 weeks PMA, and post-term 44 to 48 weeks PMA; the literal wording overlaps at 44 weeks and does not state whether 48 weeks is inclusive.
Record neuroactive medications and ideally administration times, including sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, anesthetics, and antiseizure drugs.
Record hypothermia depth, duration, and whether spontaneous or induced; record major hemodynamic, respiratory, or cardiorespiratory changes.
Record hours uninterpretable for technical reasons; characterize the first hour, one background hour in each later 24-hour period, and additional epochs after relevant change.
Record seizure onset, burden, resolution, and status epilepticus onset and resolution.
context: Every neonatal recording and each reported 24-hour period.
pitfalls: A waveform-only example without PMA and recording context cannot satisfy this contract.
engineering: Pending Craig: encode term as the half-open interval [37,44) weeks and post-term as beginning at 44 weeks; the upper 48-week boundary remains unresolved.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Behavioral state and sleep-wake cycling
definition: State assignment combines EEG and polysomnographic behavior and is interpreted relative to PMA.
criteria: A state requires its defining features for >=60 seconds.

Allowed states are awake, active sleep, quiet sleep, transitional sleep, and indeterminate sleep; transitional sleep mixes features of the states on either side, while indeterminate sleep cannot be assigned to active or quiet sleep.
Term awake and active sleep use continuous low-to-medium voltage mixed-frequency activité moyenne; active sleep additionally has closed eyes, REM, irregular respiration, and body movement.
Term quiet sleep has closed eyes, absent REM, little movement, and near term commonly tracé alternant; mature continuous high-voltage slow activity and 10-12 Hz spindles emerge around 46 weeks PMA.

Sleep-wake cycling records orderly alteration among states: term complete sleep-wake cycles are typically 3-4 hours and sleep-only cycles 40-70 minutes; preterm sleep cycles are 30-50 minutes below 35 weeks PMA and 50-65 minutes beyond 35 weeks PMA.
Unspecified state change requires distinct EEG patterns differing in discontinuity, voltage, or frequency, with each state lasting >=60 seconds.
context: Neonatal recordings with sufficient EEG, eye, respiratory, movement, and preferably EMG observations.
pitfalls: Do not force active or quiet sleep when clinical and EEG features are insufficient or discordant.
A short page cannot establish sleep-wake cycling.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Normal continuity, tracé discontinu, and tracé alternant
definition: Normal neonatal continuity and discontinuity are PMA- and state-dependent rather than fixed adult categories.
criteria: Continuous activity has no interruption and <2 seconds of attenuation below 25 µV peak-to-peak.
An interburst interval (IBI) is attenuation below an age-dependent level described broadly as <25-50 µV peak-to-peak for >=2 seconds; Table 1 supplies the age bins.
Normal maximum IBI/voltage by PMA: <30 weeks, 35 seconds and <25 µV; 30-33 weeks, 20 seconds and <25 µV; 34-36 weeks, 10 seconds and approximately 25 µV; 37-40 weeks, 6 seconds and >25 µV.

Tracé discontinu contains 50-300 µV bursts with low-voltage IBIs and age-appropriate graphoelements; it is developmentally expected mainly from 26-40 weeks PMA and becomes confined to quiet sleep with maturation.

Tracé alternant occurs only in quiet sleep: 50-150 µV delta bursts lasting roughly 4-10 seconds alternate with 25-50 µV mixed theta-delta periods that never fall below 25 µV; it appears around 34-36 weeks, is minimal by 42 weeks, and is absent by 46 weeks PMA.
context: Background assessment in preterm, term, and post-term neonates.
pitfalls: Do not label age-appropriate discontinuity excessive using a fixed IBI threshold.
The source gives no Table 1 normal IBI row above 40 weeks PMA.

name: Excessive discontinuity and neonatal burst suppression
definition: Separates PMA-inappropriate discontinuity that retains normal elements from invariant burst suppression lacking normal graphoelements.
criteria: Excessive discontinuity has IBIs too long or too voltage-depressed for PMA while bursts retain some age-appropriate patterns or graphoelements.
Burst suppression has invariant abnormal bursts separated by prolonged IBIs with voltage <5 µV peak-to-peak.

Permitted activity within burst-suppression IBIs is limited to sparse activity up to 15 µV in one electrode, transient activity up to 15 µV for <2 seconds, or the source-described >2:1 voltage asymmetry in multiple electrodes.

Burst suppression is unreactive and lacks spontaneous lability; bursts lack recognizable normal graphoelements and should be described as >100 µV or <100 µV, with typical burst and IBI durations and burst-component sharpness recorded.
context: Discontinuous neonatal backgrounds assessed against PMA and state.
pitfalls: Do not call a variable or reactive record with normal graphoelements burst suppression.
Do not infer severity from discontinuity without PMA and state.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Background symmetry and interhemispheric synchrony
definition: Symmetry compares homologous content and voltage; synchrony compares burst onset timing and has a non-linear developmental course.
criteria: Persistent >2:1 voltage difference between homologous regions, or persistent disparity in frequency or graphoelement distribution, is abnormal asymmetry; fleeting differences may remain normal.
A burst pair is synchronous when left and right onsets differ by <=1.5 seconds; report the percentage of synchronous bursts.
Near-complete synchrony is expected before roughly 27-29 weeks and again near term; about 70% synchrony may occur around 29-30 weeks and some asynchrony is expected from 30-37 weeks.
After 38 weeks PMA, substantial asynchrony is not expected; abnormal asynchrony means a clearly excessive PMA-adjusted proportion of bursts with onset difference >1.5 seconds.
context: Multichannel neonatal background, with synchrony assessed during discontinuous portions.
pitfalls: Synchrony does not describe continuous portions without identifiable bursts.
No universal abnormal percentage cutoff is supplied; judgment remains PMA-conditioned.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Term background voltage and electrocerebral inactivity
definition: Voltage categories for term neonatal background plus the separately standardized technical claim of electrocerebral inactivity (ECI).
criteria: Normal term background has most activity >=25 µV peak-to-peak in every behavioral state.
Borderline low voltage is continuous, retains normal activity and graphoelements, and is persistently >=10 and <25 µV peak-to-peak.
Low-voltage suppressed background lacks normal features, has fundamental baseline <10 µV peak-to-peak, permits >=10 µV transients only when <2 seconds, and is invariant and unreactive.

ECI means no discernible cerebral activity at or above 2 µV peak-to-peak when reviewed at sensitivity 2 µV/mm and only when ECI technical standards were met; otherwise report only that the record may be consistent with ECI.
context: Voltage categories apply primarily to term infants; ECI requires a recording performed to separate ECI technical standards.
pitfalls: The source declines to define normal voltage limits for premature infants.
Do not determine cerebral death from this EEG term alone.
Do not apply ECI after a standard neonatal acquisition that lacks ECI technical requirements.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Background variability and reactivity
definition: Variability is spontaneous change from internal state; reactivity is cerebral EEG change after external stimulation.
criteria: A qualifying response is a conspicuous change in frequency, continuity, or voltage.
Record each feature as yes, no, or unclear/unknown/not applicable.
Variability first appears near 25 weeks PMA, increases by 28 weeks, and is well established around 30-31 weeks.
Reactivity first appears around 30-32 weeks PMA; record stimulus type and strength.
Separate cerebral change from movement, EMG, crying, and respiratory artifacts; arousal-related voltage attenuation is not automatically discontinuity.
context: Neonatal background with sufficient longitudinal state sampling and documented stimulation.
pitfalls: Behavioral or muscle response alone is not cerebral EEG reactivity.
Absence during one short state sample does not establish global absence.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: EEG dysmaturity
definition: The EEG background appears developmentally appropriate for an infant at least two weeks younger than the actual PMA.
criteria: Difference between actual PMA and EEG-implied PMA is >=2 weeks.
Persistent dysmaturity is abnormal; the source frames the concept longitudinally.
context: Serial or sufficiently comprehensive neonatal recordings with an assigned EEG maturational age.
pitfalls: Do not infer dysmaturity from one isolated feature without an overall maturational assessment.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Normal neonatal graphoelements
definition: Named developmental background hallmarks whose morphology, state, distribution, and expected PMA window jointly determine normality.
criteria: Monorhythmic delta: 24-34 weeks PMA, up to 200 µV peak-to-peak, stereotyped delta usually occipital, temporal, or central and rarely frontal; typically symmetric, synchronous, and often surface positive.

Delta brushes: most prominent 24-36 weeks, 0.3-1.5 Hz slow waves at 50-250 µV with superimposed 8-12 or 18-22 Hz activity; peak expression 32-34 weeks, with state distribution changing by PMA and occasional quiet-sleep occurrence through 40 weeks.

Rhythmic temporal theta: 24-34 weeks, 25-120 µV theta in approximately 2-second temporal bursts, typically symmetric and maximal at 29-32 weeks; similar activity may occur at vertex or occipital sites.
Anterior dysrhythmia: 32-44 weeks, 50-100 µV frontal delta waves singly or in brief runs, typically symmetric and synchronous.

Encoches frontales: 34-44 weeks, 50-100 µV broad diphasic frontal transients lasting 0.5-0.75 seconds with small initial negative and larger positive phase; typically symmetric/synchronous and enriched during transition from active to quiet sleep.
context: Neonatal background interpreted with PMA and state.
pitfalls: A named morphology outside its PMA/state/distribution context is not automatically a normal graphoelement.
The source states that its list is not exhaustive.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Neonatal sharp-wave transients
definition: Distinct positive or negative transients are classified using baseline duration, abundance, spatial distribution, repetition, PMA, and background context.
criteria: A spike lasts <100 ms at baseline; a sharp wave lasts 100-200 ms; the transient must stand apart from background rather than be only sharply contoured background.

Physiologic negative sharp waves are usually 100-200 ms, solitary, symmetric, and mid-temporal/central/centro-temporal against a PMA-normal background; frontal, vertex, and occipital locations are uncommon.

Abnormal negative transients are supported by abnormal background, concentration in one region or hemisphere, atypical location, high abundance, or repetitive runs; source-cited outcome data call rates >11/hour preterm and >13/hour term abnormal.

Positive Rolandic/vertex sharp waves are centered at C3/C4 or vertex with adjacent field; excessive positive mid-temporal waves can indicate focal pathology, while cited upper normal observations are 3/hour preterm and 1.5/hour term.
context: Transient assessment in the most continuous portions of neonatal EEG, preferably wakefulness or active sleep.
pitfalls: Do not count fleeting sharp contour embedded in discontinuous bursts as a distinct transient.
Abundance boundaries remain debated and the cited rates are not presented as a complete standalone diagnostic rule.

name: Brief rhythmic discharge
definition: An evolving rhythmic neonatal discharge resembling seizure activity but lasting less than ten seconds.
criteria: Rhythmic electrical activity shows evolution and duration <10 seconds.
Record accompanying background abnormality and confirmed seizures; these are common contexts but not stated as mandatory criteria.
context: Neonatal evolving rhythmic events below seizure duration.
pitfalls: An event lasting >=10 seconds may meet neonatal seizure criteria instead.
A very brief rhythmic pattern without evolution belongs with non-seizure rhythmic/periodic patterns, not BRD.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Neonatal seizure type, electrographic definition, and spread
definition: A neonatal electrographic seizure is a sudden abnormal repetitive evolving EEG event meeting voltage and duration thresholds; clinical coupling is classified separately.
criteria: Electrographic seizure is repetitive and unequivocally evolves in frequency, voltage, morphology, or location, reaches >=2 µV peak-to-peak, and lasts >=10 seconds; there is no minimum electrical frequency.
The 2 µV threshold marks seizure beginning and end; two events are separate only when the inter-event interval is >=10 seconds.
Electroclinical seizure has definite simultaneous clinical seizure signs; electrographic-only seizure has no specific visible clinical sign; clinical-only events have no simultaneous EEG seizure.

Spread classes are diffuse asynchronous involvement of all electrodes, bilateral independent, migrating between hemispheres, lateralized within one hemisphere, unifocal onset, or multifocal onset from >=3 independent foci with >=1 in each hemisphere.
Restricted locations may be frontal, central, temporal, occipital, vertex, anterior quadrant, posterior quadrant, or hemispheric left/right.
context: Neonatal EEG events with calibrated voltage, continuous duration, evolution, and clinical/video correlation when a clinical class is assigned.
pitfalls: Do not call evolving activity <10 seconds a seizure; use BRD.
Do not call repetitive activity without evolution a seizure even when >10 seconds.
Do not confuse arousal or drowsiness background transitions with seizures.
Do not use generalized synchronous terminology where the neonatal source specifies diffuse asynchronous spread.
status: Source-extracted draft · clinical editorial review pending

name: Neonatal seizure burden and status epilepticus
definition: Seizure burden is quantified over an explicit denominator; neonatal status is defined by seizure occupancy of a one-hour epoch.
criteria: Clinical burden may be reported as seizure count per hour or total seizure duration divided by the duration of the epoch of interest.

Research temporal-spatial burden sums seizure duration per hour in five non-overlapping neonatal montage regions so each electrode is counted once; the source lists Fp3-T3, C3-O1, Fp4-T4, C4-O2, Fz-Pz or an alternate pairing.
Status epilepticus is present when summed seizure duration is >=50% of any defined 60-minute epoch.
context: Continuous neonatal EEG with complete seizure start/stop annotations and a defined analysis epoch.
pitfalls: Do not report a percentage without the epoch denominator.
The source explicitly describes the 50% status cutoff as somewhat arbitrary rather than outcome-validated.

name: Neonatal rhythmic and periodic patterns of uncertain significance
definition: Non-seizure periodic discharges and rhythmic delta activity are described by waveform organization, minimum cycles, onset, spread, and neonatal location terms.
criteria: Periodic discharges have relatively uniform morphology/duration, a measurable interdischarge interval, and near-regular recurrence: cycle length varies <50% between adjacent cycles in >50% of cycle pairs.
A discharge has <=3 phases or lasts <=0.5 seconds regardless of phases; a burst lasts >0.5 seconds and has >=4 phases.
RDA repeats relatively uniform waveforms without an inter-wave interval and has cycle-length variation <50% in >50% of adjacent cycle pairs.
PD or RDA must persist for >=6 cycles.

Location is lateralized, diffuse with asynchronous all-electrode involvement, bilateral independent, or multifocal; report onset focus, maximal spread, and F/C/T/O/Z or hemispheric predominance as applicable.
For diffuse patterns, frontal, occipital, or midline predominance requires amplitude >=50% greater than the comparison region in an appropriate referential montage.
context: Neonatal rhythmic or periodic patterns that do not have seizure-defining evolution.
pitfalls: Evolution is not an RPP modifier in neonates because evolution defines BRD or seizure according to duration.
Neonatal RDA is not necessarily abnormal; normal rhythmic occipital delta and anterior dysrhythmia can meet rhythmic form.

name: Neonatal rhythmic/periodic duration, polarity, and sharpness modifiers
definition: Neonatal RPPs use a limited modifier set with neonatal duration boundaries and bipolar polarity measurement.
criteria: Record typical duration and preferably longest continuous duration: very long >=1 hour; long 5-59 minutes; intermediate 1-4.9 minutes; brief 10-59 seconds; very brief <10 seconds without evolution.
Determine predominant-phase polarity in a traditional bipolar montage as positive, negative, or unclear.

Measure sharpness at baseline for predominant and sharpest phase: spiky <100 ms; sharp 100-200 ms; sharply contoured theta/delta is >200 ms with steep or pointed morphology; blunt is smooth or sinusoidal.
context: Non-continuous neonatal PD/RDA patterns; polarity and sharpness apply only to PDs and the spike/sharp component of spike-wave patterns, not RDA.
pitfalls: Do not apply polarity or sharpness to RDA.
Do not use the newer non-neonatal 10-59 minute long-duration boundary; S09 specifies 5-59 minutes.
Very brief evolving events are BRDs, not static RPP duration examples.
